title: Why Do Bananas Turn Brown in Just 5 Seconds?

scenes.text: Bananas brown in just 5 seconds after a bite – why?
Polyphenol oxidase in banana cells reacts with oxygen, creating brown pigments called melanin.
When the fruit is cut, cells release air‑filled spaces, letting oxygen flood the flesh and speed up the reaction.
The brown layer actually shields the fruit, acting as an antioxidant barrier that slows deeper damage.
